# Dependencies are scanned for known vulnerabilities in CI

> Source: `docs/security-review-2026-11-01.md` (SK-SEC-08), PR #70.

## Context and Problem Statement

The router and the agent depend on Python and Go packages. Nothing checked them for known vulnerabilities; two Go modules
(the MQTT client and `golang.org/x/net`) were behind.

## Decision Drivers

* Learn about vulnerable dependencies without manual checks.
* Keep lock files generated by the language tooling, not edited by hand.

## Considered Options

* A security workflow running `govulncheck` (Go) and `pip-audit` (Python), plus Dependabot for update pull requests
* Manual review at release time
* A commercial scanning service

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: "`govulncheck`, `pip-audit` and Dependabot", because they are the languages' own tools, run in the
existing CI without accounts, and Dependabot proposes updates as pull requests that go through the normal review.

### Consequences

* Good, because a vulnerable dependency shows up as a failing check or a pull request.
* Bad, because a newly published vulnerability can turn the CI red without a code change; it then has to be fixed or
  explicitly accepted.

### Confirmation

`.github/workflows/security.yml` (jobs `go-security`, `python-security`) and `.github/dependabot.yml`.
